cloud_text.title: Send text to the cloud?
blocks: The text you dictated or selected, up to 5,000 characters a request. Never your voice.
Groq and/or Google — repair, punctuation, translation, lookup, the second reading.
Your own key. You are their customer; nothing passes through a DeskIT server.

Groq: "not permitted to use Inputs or Outputs for training"; nothing kept by default. 18+. Google (Gemini, free tier): used "to provide, improve, and develop Google products"; humans may read it. Not for the EU, UK or Switzerland. 18+.
Settings > Privacy, or remove the key.
cloud_text.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.

cloud_audio.title: Send recordings to the cloud?
blocks: The recording of what you just said, as a WAV file.
Your own key. You are their customer; nothing passes through a DeskIT server.

Google (Gemini, free tier): used "to provide, improve, and develop Google products"; humans may read it. Not for the EU, UK or Switzerland. 18+. Groq: "not permitted to use Inputs or Outputs for training"; nothing kept by default. 18+.
Settings > Privacy, or remove the key. The engine goes back to local.
cloud_audio.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.

cloud_screenshots.title: Send a screenshot to the cloud?
blocks: A JPEG of the area you marked, your question, and the earlier questions on the same card. A screenshot can hold mail, a bank, anything that was on screen.
Groq and/or Google, for the question about the screen.
Your own key. You are their customer; nothing passes through a DeskIT server.

Groq: "not permitted to use Inputs or Outputs for training"; nothing kept by default. 18+. Google (Gemini, free tier): used "to provide, improve, and develop Google products"; humans may read it. Not for the EU, UK or Switzerland. 18+.
Settings > Privacy, or remove the key.
cloud_screenshots.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.

account.title: Open an account?
blocks: An account id — anonymous, or the e-mail of the Google account you chose; this PC's name; the app, Windows and hardware versions.
DeskIT's server (Supabase, Frankfurt) — the only server DeskIT has.
DeskIT's project; your keys never travel there — they have no column in the database.
The one-page terms and the privacy policy.
account.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.

report_upload.title: Send problem reports?
blocks: Only what the report's preview showed — after the clean-up.
DeskIT's server (Supabase, Frankfurt) — the only server DeskIT has.
DeskIT's project, through your anonymous account.
The one-page terms and the privacy policy.
Keep it on this PC instead, or Settings > Privacy > Withdraw.
report_upload.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.

settings_sync.title: Sync settings and words?
blocks: Your settings changes and the words you taught it — never keys, hotkeys, devices, folders or positions; never audio, history or reports.
DeskIT's server (Supabase, Frankfurt) — the only server DeskIT has. From there to every PC you sign in on.
The one-page terms and the privacy policy.
settings_sync.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.

history_sync.title: Sync what you said?
blocks: Everything you dictated, translated, punctuated and looked up — the text, not the recording — so the Said page is the same on every PC.
DeskIT's server (Supabase, Frankfurt) — the only server DeskIT has. Kept in your account; DeskIT's key can technically read it — the protection separates users, not the project's admin.
The one-page terms and the privacy policy.
Settings > Privacy > Withdraw; "Delete my account" removes what was synced too.
history_sync.footer: Every connection DeskIT makes is listed under Settings > Privacy > Every connection, and in network.log.
